items.title: David Brinkley Interview, 1962-01-10
items.q: The mention of Stalin occurs in a commercial break/promo for a news program ('In Stalingrad, the plaques of Stalin have been chiseled from the walls...'), not in the interviewee's personal narrative or interaction.

ctx.x: Back in 1947, there just wasn't any jazz here. The only way you could hear it was to play your old 78 records. So that's what we did, until we got brave enough to have our own little concert. Then we started from there.

Go, get it! Yeah! Don't make no difference, huh? That's fine! Go, go, go! Go, go, go! Go, go, go! Go, go, go, go! Go, go, go, go! Used to have dozens of marching bands for parades, funerals, and picnics. Now, there are four. Grand Marshal of the parade is Matthew Fats Houston, a drummer by trade who seldom works at. One of the marching bands New Orleans no longer has was led by Papa Jack Lane, now 89 years old, the oldest of the older generation of musicians still left. He is a drummer.
